title: Interlink Electronics Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
summary: Pending transformative acquisition expected to close in Q4. Third-quarter 2026 revenue increased 3% to $3.06 million, and the net loss narrowed to $316,000 from $336,000 a year earlier.
body_markdown:
Pending Transformative Acquisition Expected to Close in Q4


FREMONT, Calif., Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Interlink Electronics, Inc. (Nasdaq: LINK) (“Interlink” or the “Company”), a global leader in sensor technology and printed electronic solutions, today reported its results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


Pending Transformative Acquisition


Subject to satisfactory completion of due diligence, execution of all necessary documentation, and availability of financing, we currently anticipate that the acquisition described in our May 11, 2026 release will close before year-end. This transformative transaction is projected to result in a combined $50 million in revenue and over $4 million in Adjusted EBITDA for 2026 on a pro forma basis.


Q3 2026 Highlights


We established a new 4,000-square-foot R&D center for next-generation smart functional textiles at the Advanced Manufacturing Park (AMP) in Rotherham, UK. The center will drive research, product development, and rapid prototyping using our award-winning Conductive Transfer process to build solutions that integrate sensors, microelectronics, and embedded intelligence for smart textile applications. Interlink joins a prestigious ecosystem at the AMP alongside industry leaders like Boeing, Rolls-Royce, and McLaren Automotive.


We also added a 10,000-square-foot facility adjacent to our Irvine, Scotland footprint, dedicated to high-volume conductive transfer printing and high-volume printed electrodes for medical and diagnostics applications. This expansion will enable us to serve the emerging opportunities in both the medical and wearables markets.


“We continue to invest in our business and take the necessary steps to drive long-term growth,” said Steven N. Bronson, Chairman, President, and CEO. “We feel confident that our existing technologies and capabilities, coupled with adding additional sales and marketing resources, will position us for organic growth in the coming years.”


Consolidated Financial Results


Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 increased 3% to $3.06 million, compared to $2.96 million in the third quarter of 2025, and for the first nine months of 2026 increased 10% to $9.90 million, compared to $9.04 million in the first nine months of 2025. The revenue increase for the quarter was driven by higher shipments of our force-sensing and gas-sensor products, partially offset by lower sales of our Calman printed electronics products. The revenue increase for the first nine months of the year was driven by higher shipments of our force-sensing products, partially offset by lower sales of our gas-sensor and Calman printed electronics products. Revenues fluctuate periodically in response to changes in customer demand, which can vary with order flow and production cycles, affecting both the timing and volume of shipments.


Gross margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 37.3%, a decrease from 41.8% for the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in gross margin was due to higher materials and production expenses for our Calman printed electronics products, and changes in the mix of our products and services. Gross margin for the first nine months of 2026 was 41.9%, compared with 41.2% for the first nine months of 2025. The slight increase in gross margin was due to higher revenue and changes in the mix of our products and services.


Net income/loss for the third quarter of 2026 was a loss of $316,000, compared to a loss of $336,000 in same quarter last year, and for the first nine months of 2026 was a loss of $406,000, compared to a loss of $1,041,000 in the first nine months of 2025. The improvement in net income/loss for the nine-month period was driven primarily by higher revenue and lower operating expenses.


Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure, for the third quarter of 2026 was $(176,000), versus $(61,000) in the same quarter last year, and for the first nine months of 2026 was $79,000, versus $(361,000) in the first nine months of 2025.


The full release, including the condensed consolidated balance sheets, statements of operations, and the reconciliation of net income (loss) to Adjusted EBITDA, is available via the source link above.


About Interlink Electronics, Inc.


Interlink Electronics is a leading provider of sensors and printed electronic solutions, boasting 40 years of success in delivering mission-critical technologies across diverse markets. Our customers, including global blue-chip companies, trust our products and solutions, which span various markets, including medical, industrial, automotive, wearables, IoT, and other specialty markets. Our expertise in materials science, manufacturing, embedded electronics, firmware, and software enables us to create custom solutions tailored to our customers’ unique needs.


We serve our international customer base from our corporate headquarters and proprietary gas sensor production and product development facility in Fremont, California (Silicon Valley area); our advanced printed-electronics manufacturing center in Shenzhen, China; and our multiple facilities in Irvine, Scotland, and our smart textile and wearables product development footprint located in the Evolution Advanced Manufacturing Park in Rotherham, England.


For more information, please visit www.InterlinkElectronics.com.

Non-GAAP Financial Measure


To supplement our condensed consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), we use the following non-GAAP financial measure: Adjusted EBITDA. The presentation of this financial information is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP. We define Adjusted EBITDA for a particular period as net income (loss) before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, and as further adjusted for stock-based compensation expense.


We use this non-GAAP financial measure for financial and operational decision-making and as a means to evaluate period-to-period comparisons. We believe that this non-GAAP financial measure provides meaningful supplemental information regarding our performance by excluding certain items that may not be indicative of our core business operating results, such as amortization expense related to our recent acquisitions. We believe that both management and investors benefit from referring to this non-GAAP financial measure in assessing our performance and when planning, forecasting, and analyzing future periods. This non-GAAP financial measure also facilitates management’s internal comparisons to our historical performance and liquidity as well as comparisons to our competitors’ operating results. We believe this non-GAAP financial measure is useful to investors both because (1) it allows for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in its financial and operational decision-making and (2) it is used by our investors to help them analyze the health of our business.


There are a number of limitations related to the use of non-GAAP financial measures. We compensate for these limitations by providing specific information regarding the GAAP amounts excluded from these non-GAAP financial measures and evaluating these non-GAAP financial measures together with their relevant financial measures in accordance with GAAP.
